newsitem.title: USA: Olin sees better pricing, demand.
newsitem.headline: Olin sees better pricing, demand.

text.p: Olin Corp said Thursday that it expects that tight supply-demand will increase pricing for its chlor alkali products and that demand will accelerate for its microelectronic materials as the year progresses.
Olin reported second quarter earnings of $0.75 a share, compared to $1.01 a share the previous second quarter.

"Our second quarter results primarily reflect lower pricing in the chlor alkali industry, slower than anticipated recovery in certain microelectronic material markets, and the absence of earnings from our TDI and ADI businesses which were divested last year," said Donald Griffin, chairman, president and chief executive officer said in a press release.
Olin said it is well positioned for future earnings growth when demand and pricing improve in its key markets.
Chemicals segment operating income was $46 million in the second quarter of 1997, compared with $65.7 million as reported for 1996, and $56.2 million excluding the TDI/ADI isocyanates business.
Metals and ammunition operating income was $12.6 million, compared with $14.0 million.

The company also said that after an extensive review of options regarding the businesses and assets at its Brandenburg, Kentucky site, it has concluded that maximum economic value would be realized from the retention of its non-foam polyol business.
